model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 total revenues (Q4-2025 supplement, 8-K ex99.2 0000074208-26-000009; ties to XBRL). The engine's 'ebitda_margin_path' is the AFFO margin on this revenue line, not EBITDA. FY2025 AFFO $792.6M = 46.3% of revenue. FY2026E: FFOA guidance midpoint $2.53 x 348.5M weighted diluted shares+units = $881.7M, less ~$115M recurring capex (H1-26 $49.2M; FY25 $113.8M, H2-weighted) = ~$767M AFFO on ~$1,691M revenue (H1-26 $851.2M actual, H2 lighter after $400-750M of guided dispositions) = 45.3%.
inputs.share_count_basis: Total common shares, OP/DownREIT units and common stock equivalents at 30 June 2026 = 346,186,551 (Q2-2026 supplement Attachment 4(A)): 321.27M common + 0.12M restricted equivalents + 21.98M OP/DownREIT units + 2.82M Series E convertible preferred as-converted. AFFO 'attributable to common stockholders and unitholders, diluted' adds back the Series E distributions and OP-unit NCI, so the divisor must include both. Held FLAT: SBC is already expensed inside FFO/AFFO (NAREIT FFO does not add it back), and the ongoing buyback (25.5M shares of authorisation left) is funded by dispositions that also remove revenue; leaving both out is roughly neutral and mildly conservative while the stock trades below private-market value.
inputs.net_debt_note: Held at ZERO in the engine by design: AFFO is a post-interest, post-preferred flow capitalised at the cost of equity, so deducting the $5,812.6M net debt again would double-count it. The refinancing of that debt is charged in the AFFO margin path instead (see assumptions.base.ebitda_margin_note). Actual balance sheet recorded in debt_memo.

debt_memo.maturities_2026_2031: 808 / 318 / 467 / 966 / 831 / 761 ($M), 71% of the stack rolls by end-2031 at an average in-place coupon of ~3.5%
debt_memo.source: Q2-2026 supplement (8-K ex99.2, 0000074208-26-000070) Attachment 4(B)/4(C) debt structure, maturities and net-debt reconciliation

inputs.fcf_definition: AFFO attributable to common stockholders and unitholders, diluted, FY2025 = FFO as Adjusted $906.4M less recurring capex (incl. JV share) $113.8M (Q4-2025 supplement). Already after interest, preferred dividends, SBC and recurring capex. Redevelopment, NOI-enhancing and development capex are growth capital funded from retained AFFO (~22% after the $1.74 dividend), disposition proceeds and debt; they are what the revenue path pays for and are not deducted again. GAAP OCF ($902.9M FY25) is not used.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 cash-flow add-back $26.5M (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation, UDR_Metrics.csv). Memo only: NAREIT FFO and UDR's FFOA/AFFO do NOT add SBC back, so it is already expensed in last_fcf and deducted zero times more. House and street bases coincide; band_position is null.
inputs.buyback_note: H1-2026 repurchases ~$300M: $100M Q1 (XBRL) + $200.3M Q2 (5.5M shares at $36.49, Q2-2026 release). Since recommencing in Sept 2025: 11.5M shares for $418.0M at $36.32. FY2025 $117.8M. Funded largely by dispositions (FY26 guide $400-750M at share).
inputs.horizon_note: FY0 is FY2025 actual; year 1 is FY2026 (guided), years 2-10 are FY2027-FY2035. The valuation date is nine months into FY2026, so discounting the full FY2026 AFFO a full year is mildly conservative.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC, because the capitalised flow is post-interest. USD build: 10-year US Treasury 5.24% (2026-10-01, as used for MAA the same day), equity risk premium 4.5%, beta 0.90 -> 5.24 + 0.90 x 4.5 = 9.3%, rounded to 9.25%. Beta set 0.05 above the MAA build (0.85) because UDR carries more leverage (5.6x net debt/EBITDAre vs MAA 4.5x; 3.9 vs 6.0 years to maturity) and coastal rent-regulation exposure. Cross-check: at the current price the stock yields ~5.2% on the $1.74 dividend and ~6.6% on FY26E AFFO (~15x P/AFFO); 9.25% CoE with 2.5% terminal growth implies a 15.2x steady-state AFFO multiple, in line with 2023-2026 apartment-REIT trading (14-18x). One rate across scenarios; risk sits in the paths and the weights, not in stacked discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable as a lessee of note: UDR is the lessor. Ground-lease expense (ROU assets $185.6M) is inside property operating expense and therefore inside AFFO; no separate lease charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: OP/DownREIT units (21.98M, $900.3M redeemable NCI at book) handled by valuing AFFO attributable to stockholders AND unitholders and dividing by shares plus units. Series E convertible preferred included as-converted (2.82M) because diluted AFFO adds back its distributions. Series F preferred is a voting share with nominal value ($1k book). Other consolidated NCI $0.3M, immaterial.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the Drivers/engine route with net debt held at zero (the MAA/GPT.AX/GMG.AX pattern). Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md 'REIT / property trust' row: UDR is a self-administered US multifamily REIT; GAAP net income is dominated by ~$680M/yr of real-estate depreciation and lumpy disposition gains (FY26 guide: $0.55/share of gains), the CSV has no capex/FCF series, and the sector is priced on FFO/AFFO and NAV, not EV/EBITDA or P/E. No dcf-methods REIT reference file exists, so the mechanics follow the same-day MAA build (the closest peer, same model) for consistency. Engine mapping: revenue = total revenues; ebitda_margin_path = AFFO margin on revenue; SBC, D&A, capex, tax and working-capital paths = 0 (all already inside AFFO, or nil for a REIT). First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry). XBRL does not carry FFO/AFFO/recurring capex; these were read from the Q4 earnings supplements (8-K ex99.2) for FY2019-FY2025 and the Q2-2026 supplement, now saved under research/UDR/Extracted/.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Judgment: 10-year AFFO/share CAGR of the base path (FY2026E ~$2.21 -> FY2035E ~$2.77). Below the 5-year AFFO/share CAGR (3.6%, flattered by the 2022 rent surge and the 2021-22 equity-funded acquisitions) and above the 3-year (1.7%, the 2023-26 supply wave plus rising interest cost); matches the 2019-2025 run-rate of ~2.5%. Book-equity CAGR is not usable for a REIT.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-7.1% 3yr, +0.2% 5yr) diverges from revenue (+4.1%/+6.7%) and EPS (+63%/+41%) by far more than 30%. Expected for a REIT: book equity is depreciated historical cost reduced by a dividend above GAAP earnings and by buybacks; GAAP EPS swings with disposition gains (FY2023 $1.34, FY2024 $0.26, FY2025 $1.13). Growth was selected from the AFFO/share series instead.
historical_growth.notes: AFFO/share has been flat for four years ($2.21 FY23, $2.19 FY24, $2.22 FY25, ~$2.20 FY26E) while revenue grew ~2-3%/yr: Sunbelt supply (Austin -5.4%, Tampa -3.6% NOI in Q2-26), opex growth above revenue growth (FY26 same-store expense +2.75-3.75% vs revenue +0.75-2.0%) and rising interest cost absorbed the top line. AFFO margin has compressed from 51.8% (FY2019) to 46.3% (FY2025). The $1.74 dividend is ~79% of FY26E AFFO.

base.growth_rates_note: FY26 -1.2%: H1 actual $851.2M plus a lighter H2 after dispositions (net seller, $400-750M sold vs $130-300M bought). FY27 +1.5%: same-store revenue ~2.5-3% (coastal blended lease growth 3.8% in Q2-26, Sunbelt still negative) net of the full-year loss of 2026 sales. FY28-29 +3.5% as Sunbelt deliveries fall below average and the 685-home development pipeline delivers 2027-29; fading to 2.5% nominal.
base.ebitda_margin_note: AFFO margin on total revenue. FY26 45.3% ties to the $2.53 FFOA midpoint less ~$115M recurring capex. Glides down 130bp to 44.0% by FY2033 because refinancing outruns operating leverage: $4.15B (71%) of the debt stack matures 2026-2031 at ~3.5% and rolls at ~5.0-5.5% (~$70-75M/yr of extra interest at full run-rate, ~4pp of revenue), and a further $1.08B of 2032-33 paper at ~2% rolls after that. Offset assumed: same-store rent growth ~50-75bp above expense growth from FY28 lifts NOI margin ~2.5-3pp over the decade, plus G&A leverage. Net -1.3pp is the judgment.
base.narrative: A flat 2026 (AFFO ~$2.21/share on the period-end count) while UDR sells ~$575M of assets and buys back stock, then a measured recovery: coastal markets keep compounding at 3-4% on constrained supply, the Sunbelt turns positive from 2027-28 as the 2023-25 delivery wave clears, and refinancing of the 3.3%-coupon stack at ~5.25% absorbs most of the operating leverage. AFFO/share ~$2.21 FY26E -> ~$2.44 FY30E -> ~$2.76 FY35E (~2.6% CAGR, the 2019-2025 run-rate). Terminal 2.5% at 9.25% CoE (~15.2x AFFO); the 18x cap does not bind.

bull.narrative: FY26 lands at the top of the raised FFOA range ($2.57); coastal blended lease growth stays near 4% and the Sunbelt supply cliff turns Austin/Tampa positive in 2027, taking same-store revenue to 4-5% for FY28-29. Long rates ease toward 4.25-4.5% so the 2026-31 maturities roll at ~4.5%, a modest cost the operating leverage (AI leasing, self-guided tours, opex discipline) more than covers; the AFFO margin rebuilds to 46%. Disposition-funded buybacks below NAV are an unmodelled extra. AFFO/share ~$2.64 FY30E, ~$3.08 FY35E; terminal 3.0% (Gordon ~16.5x, 20x cap not binding).

bear.narrative: Higher-for-longer (10-year above 5%) and a softer labour market: Sunbelt supply clears slowly while renewed starts refill the pipeline, rent control spreads beyond Washington State and Salinas into more of UDR's California/Pacific Northwest footprint, and expense growth (insurance, property tax) keeps running ahead of rents. The 2026-31 maturities roll at 5.75-6.25%, taking ~4pp off the AFFO margin by FY2033. AFFO/share troughs ~$2.15 in FY2027-29 and only reaches ~$2.34 by FY2035; valued as a 1.75% grower with a 14x cap (Gordon at 9.25%/1.75% is 13.6x, so Gordon binds).

scenario_narratives.base: A flat, net-seller 2026 (AFFO ~$2.21/share) followed by coastal-led recovery and a Sunbelt turn from 2027-28; refinancing a 3.3%-coupon, 3.9-year debt stack at ~5.25% eats most of the operating leverage, so AFFO/share compounds ~2.6% a year, the same pace as 2019-2025. Dividend stays covered at ~75-80% of AFFO.
scenario_narratives.bull: Coastal reacceleration persists, the Sunbelt supply cliff delivers two years of 4-5% same-store growth, and easier long rates let the 2026-31 maturities roll near 4.5%. The AFFO margin rebuilds to 46% and AFFO/share reaches ~$2.64 by FY2030.
scenario_narratives.bear: Rates stay above 5%, rent regulation spreads through UDR's coastal markets, opex keeps outrunning rents and debt rolls 250-300bp above the in-place coupon. AFFO/share drifts down to ~$2.15 for three years and the stock is valued as a 1.75% grower at ~13.6x; with 88% fixed-rate debt, 87% unencumbered assets and 5.2x interest cover this is an earnings problem, not a solvency one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%, matching the same-day MAA build: the dominant variables (long rates, the timing of the Sunbelt rebalance, the spread of coastal rent regulation) are outside management's control, AFFO/share has been flat for four years, and UDR runs more leverage with a shorter maturity ladder than MAA (5.6x vs 4.5x; 3.9 vs 6.0 years), which makes it more rate-sensitive. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs easier rates and a Sunbelt recovery to coincide. Not higher on bear: the Q2-26 print raised FFOA and same-store guidance, coastal blended lease growth is 3.8%, and the balance sheet is investment grade with 88% fixed-rate debt.

valuation_philosophy.summary: UDR is valued on what it can distribute - AFFO (FFO as Adjusted less recurring capex), after interest and preferred dividends - capitalised at a 9.25% USD cost of equity off a 5.24% 10-year Treasury, with net debt NOT deducted a second time; the cost of refinancing that debt is charged explicitly in the AFFO margin path. Three ten-year AFFO paths bracket the Sunbelt recovery, coastal rent regulation and the refinancing headwind. GAAP net income, EPS, P/E, EV/EBITDA and book equity are not used: ~$680M/yr of depreciation and recurring disposition gains make them structurally uninformative for an apartment REIT.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: every 50bp on the 9.25% rate moves base value roughly 7-9%; the 5.24% 10-year Treasury input is high by post-2009 standards, so the valuation is cheaper if long rates mean-revert and dearer if they do not
Refinancing: $5.8B at a 3.31% weighted coupon with 3.9 years average maturity; 71% rolls by end-2031. Each 100bp on the whole stack is ~$58M, ~7.5% of FY26E AFFO

Coastal rent regulation: Washington statewide rent control (2025) and Salinas (2024) already apply; spread to more California/Pacific Northwest jurisdictions would cap rent growth where ~65-75% of NOI sits
Sunbelt supply timing: Austin (-5.4% NOI) and Tampa (-3.6%) are still contracting; a slower clearing pushes the base path toward the bear path

Capital recycling: dispositions-for-buybacks at ~$36 are accretive only while the stock trades below private-market value; the model holds the share count flat and ignores both the lost revenue and the retired shares
Share count: 21.98M OP/DownREIT units and 2.82M as-converted Series E preferred are treated as shares (consistent with how UDR reports diluted AFFO)

NAV gap (upside risk to the model): a simple NAV at 5.25-5.5% cap rates is ~$43-46 per share (nav_cross_check), well above the AFFO-capitalised value; consensus targets ($38-45) are anchored nearer NAV. The model sides with the public-market capitalisation of the cash flow and treats NAV convergence as an unmodelled option

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 32.94-42.00, so the price sits near the bottom of its range
data_sources.financials: SEC EDGAR (CIK 74208): Q2-2026 earnings supplement and release (8-K 0000074208-26-000070, ex99.1/ex99.2) for the balance sheet, debt structure and maturities, share+unit count, AFFO and FY2026 guidance; Q4-2025 supplement (8-K 0000074208-26-000009) for FY2025 AFFO, FFOA and recurring capex; Q4 supplements filed 2020-02-11, 2021-02-09, 2022-02-08, 2023-02-06, 2024-02-06 for FY2018-FY2023 AFFO history; SEC XBRL companyfacts as carried in UDR_Metrics.csv for revenue, SBC, equity and EPS

nav_cross_check.method: Simple NAV: consolidated NOI capitalised at a range of private-market cap rates, plus non-income assets at book, less debt and other liabilities, over 346.19M shares+units. Cross-check only; not weighted into the IV.
nav_cross_check.noi_basis: Q2-26 annualised consolidated EBITDAre adjusted $1,029.7M plus ~$70M G&A (FY26 guide $65-75M) = ~$1,100M consolidated NOI (JV NOI excluded; JV carried at book instead)
nav_cross_check.other_assets_basis: JV investments $728.8M + notes receivable (DP&E) $171.7M + development at cost $147.6M + held for disposition $54.4M, book values at 30-Jun-26
nav_cross_check.liabilities_basis: total debt $5,813.8M + real-estate taxes, accrued interest, security deposits, distributions payable and AP $430.6M (operating lease liabilities excluded: the ground rent is inside NOI)
nav_cross_check.reading: At ~5.25-5.5% apartment cap rates UDR's NAV is ~$43-46, so the price trades at a ~25-30% discount to NAV, which is the case management is acting on with disposition-funded buybacks. The AFFO capitalisation (base ~$32.7) implies the public market's ~6.5% cap rate. The gap is the classic public/private REIT spread under a 5.2% 10-year; it closes either through rates falling (bull) or through continued asset sales at private values. It is NOT counted in the IV because the model already holds asset sales and buybacks out of the share count and revenue path.
